main.title: Astral Chain
main.summary: Astral Chain is a 2019 action-adventure game developed by PlatinumGames and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo Switch.

cards.heading: A game from PlatinumGames
cards.text: Astral Chain is a 2019 action-adventure game developed by PlatinumGames and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo Switch. It was directed by Takahisa Taura, who was previously lead game designer for Nier: Automata, under supervision by Devil May Cry and Bayonetta series creator Hideki Kamiya, and character designs from manga artist Masakazu Katsura.

cards.heading: Twins and their Legions
cards.text: Set in a dystopian future Earth, the game follows the events of a special police task force that protect remnants of humanity from interdimensional creatures and aberrations that invade the planet, with the story centering on the task force's two new twin recruits. Utilizing the titular Astral Chain, the twins restrain and tether the creatures, employing them in combat and investigation, referring to them as Legions. The setting of the game draws heavy inspiration from various cyberpunk manga and anime, while the gameplay combines hack and slash combat with role-playing elements and investigative open-world adventure game sections. The gameplay segments revolve heavily around the simultaneous controlling of two characters; the player character twin and their Legion.

cards.heading: Development and reception
cards.text: Astral Chain was estimated to have had a five-year long development cycle and follows a slate of previous collaborations between PlatinumGames and Nintendo, with both companies having previously worked together on titles such as The Wonderful 101 and Bayonetta 2. The game was announced February 2019 as a part of that month's Nintendo Direct presentation. Astral Chain received highly positive reviews from critics who praised its dual-character gameplay, world building, presentation, customization, and soundtrack, though it received some criticism for its usage of a silent protagonist. As of December 2022, the game has sold over 1.3 million copies worldwide.

main.summary: Gears 5 is a 2019 third-person shooter video game developed by The Coalition and published by Xbox Game Studios for Windows and Xbox One, with an enhanced Xbox Series X/S release following in November 2020.

cards.heading: Kait investigates the Locust?s origins
cards.text: Gears 5 is a 2019 third-person shooter video game developed by The Coalition and published by Xbox Game Studios for Windows and Xbox One, with an enhanced Xbox Series X/S release following in November 2020. It is the fifth main installment of the Gears of War series and the sequel to Gears of War 4. Gears 5 follows the story of Kait Diaz, who is on a journey to find out the origin of the Locust Horde, the main antagonistic faction of the Gears of War series.

cards.heading: Release and reception
cards.text: The Ultimate Edition for Gears 5 was released on September 6, 2019, while the standard edition of the game was released worldwide on September 10, 2019. Gears 5 received generally favorable reviews from critics who praised the gameplay, campaign, presentation and amount of content, but criticised the story and overall lack of innovation.

main.title: Sayonara Wild Hearts
main.subtitle: A Broken Heart Finds Its Rhythm
main.summary: On September 19, 2019, Sayonara Wild Hearts debuted on PlayStation 4, Nintendo Switch and Apple Arcade.

cards.heading: A Broken Heart Finds Its Rhythm
cards.text: Sayonara Wild Hearts is Simogo?s 2019 rhythm game, first released on September 19 for PlayStation 4, Switch and Apple Arcade. Presented as a playable pop album, it links short levels through songs, chases, duels and changing perspectives. Daniel Ols?n and Jonathan Eng composed its soundtrack, with narration by Queen Latifah.

cards.heading: A young woman becomes the Fool
cards.text: In a time near the present, there lives a young woman whose heart has been violently broken. A butterfly flies to the woman, who is resting in bed. The butterfly transports her to the alternate universe. Riding her longboard along an ethereal highway, she chases the butterfly, and upon capturing it, she transforms into a masked heroine (The Fool).

cards.heading: 23 levels of hearts, obstacles and timed actions
cards.text: Across twenty-three levels, the rider moves automatically through surreal landscapes set to pop songs. The player steers towards hearts, avoids obstacles and answers timed prompts for jumps or attacks. Other sequences change the task, including aiming a bow with an on-screen cursor. Boss encounters combine these actions, making rhythm a matter of movement as well as a correctly timed button. Scores award bronze, silver or gold rankings. A collision returns the player to a checkpoint, and repeated failures can open a way to skip the section at the cost of its possible points.

cards.heading: The Dancing Devils and the Howling Moons
cards.text: The heroine then falls through a passage and arrives in a purple and pink city. She summons a motorcycle (Wheel of Fortune), and begins to ride through it. Weaving through cars, trams and buildings, she meets a trio of devil-masked women, the Dancing Devils. They fight on the street, before riding through the city on motorcycles. She chases and defeats each member of the trio in turn, and takes back their hearts. The Fool then travels to a mythical forest. With the help of a white stag (The Emperor), she rides through the forest and meets the Howling Moons, a quartet of wolf-masked gangsters.

main.title: Untitled Goose Game
main.subtitle: The Power of Being a Nuisance
main.summary: Untitled Goose Game lets a troublesome goose steal objects, honk and disrupt routines in a small English village.

cards.heading: A goose disturbs the village
cards.text: Untitled Goose Game is House House?s 2019 comedy game, published by Panic. Released on September 20 for Switch and computers, it puts players in control of a goose with a list of troublesome tasks. Stealing objects, making noise and interfering with villagers creates the situations needed to complete them.

cards.heading: Learning the villagers? routines
cards.text: Villagers follow routines, notice misplaced belongings and try to recover stolen objects. Watching those habits helps the player arrange a distraction or lure someone away. Moving one object can trigger reactions from several people.

cards.heading: Grabbing, honking and moving
cards.text: The goose can walk, grab things and honk. Its posture, neck movements and gait help turn these simple actions into jokes. Players use the same small set of controls in different locations, experimenting with what the residents will do.

cards.heading: Piano accompaniment follows the action
cards.text: Debussy-based piano music reacts to the action. Chases receive faster accompaniment, while quieter passages leave room for waiting and observation. The score supports the timing of the goose?s movements and the villagers? responses.
